correctness.rationale: For every nonempty finite two-equivalence structure, the indicated side-labelled incidence multigraph has one edge per element. The round-colour induction gives exact rooted alternation-unfolding types after removal of one marked element per class multiset. In a forest these unfoldings reproduce both sides of the original edge-rooted component; a cyclic incidence multigraph has arbitrarily deep nonbacktracking alternations and cannot match an n-edge forest through depth n+1. Equal edge-rooted component multisets force equal component multiplicities, hence isomorphism. Each colour is expressible in C^2 with counting, giving rank at most n+2. The exact-code checker corroborates all partition pairs through n=8, but is not used to prove the theorem.

Scheidt and Schweikardt, arXiv:2407.16022 abstract: relational colour refinement recognizes structures through homomorphisms from acyclic relational structures; the algorithm is distinct from the present separate two-equivalence edge-neighbour counts.
The incidence forest itself is bipartite, but the binary E,F relational Gaifman graph contains cliques of unbounded size.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Forest amenability is the closest stronger-looking standard theorem, but it applies to refinement on vertices of the incidence graph. The present logic quantifies only over edges, encoded as elements, and has no incidence-class vertices. A new explicit marked-edge subtraction/unfolding lemma establishes the needed transfer. Relational colour-refinement work may eventually supply a more general conceptual explanation; the searched abstract does not directly imply this theorem without an additional reduction.

value.rationale: The class of finite pairs of equivalence relations is a natural model-theoretic setting; its intersection incidence multigraph exposes tree-like geometry not apparent in a Gaifman graph full of cliques. The theorem gives an all-size isomorphism-identification result with a concrete logical-depth bound and identifies precisely the stable orbit partition. It explains a structural mechanism for why classwise neighbour counts suffice and has potential use in canonical comparison and finite-model descriptions; it is not a mere arbitrary finite cutoff or numeric table.
